value.text: Round 5 re-review plan (head 78dae97, 7 findings). Rules per finding: (1) ci.yml root engines floor — every committed lock the runtime installs gets an engine-strict check at the Node floor; add the root strict install beside the private-runtime one plus structural+behavioral tests. (2) alert fallback dedupe — fallback issue lookup keys on the workflow run identity, not the exact fallback title, so an alert issue that references the failed run (documented contract) suppresses duplication; docs updated. (3) npm bootstrap cache — a package install whose bytes the process executes must not read a cache another local user can pre-populate; replace the fixed shared temp cache with a fresh private mkdtemp cache, always removed. (4) alert test gains the ready/successful-install/failing-script fallback case. (5) install scanner — a value-taking npm option before the subcommand must not hide an install; extend the value-flag set with npm 11 string configs and add corpus cases. (6) installer matrix gains a bootstrap-succeeds-without-CLI case asserting refusal before ci plus cleanup. (7) runtime npm fixture — the Node twin must be creatable without Windows file-symlink privilege; hardlink with copy fallback on win32, symlink elsewhere, plus an executable-twin assertion. Windows CI is the revert witness for (7) since Linux cannot deny symlink privilege.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Round 5 fixes and revert proofs (all focused tests on Node 24.19.0): (1) private cache: scripts/release-runtime.ts now bootstraps and installs through a fresh mkdtemp cache (0700) removed on every outcome; reverting to the fixed shared temp cache fails the installer matrix (the fixture's cache recorder ENOENTs on the no-longer-created shared path, and the fresh/private/cleanup assertions fail); restored, 4/4 pass. (2) value-taking options: npm-bootstrap-contract VALUE_FLAGS now carries npm 11 string configs (install-strategy, audit-level, depth, cpu, os, libc, archive, save-prefix, scope, lockfile-version, fetch-*, max-sockets, proxy family, user-agent, local-address, ca/cert/key, git, editor, to/from, search*, node-options); removing install-strategy alone makes the adversarial corpus accept 'npm --install-strategy nested ci' (Missing expected exception, 1 fail); restored, 33/33 pass. (3) alert dedupe: the fallback lookup keys on the run identity (in:title,body <run id>) so a caller alert issue with any title that names the run suppresses the fallback; reverting to exact-title lookup fails the 'deduplicate on the workflow run identity' assertion; restored, 1/1 pass. (4) root engine floor: ci.yml gains 'Check root dependency engines at the Node floor' (strict root install at 22.18.0) beside the private-runtime gate, with structural (both strict gates at the floor) and behavioral (real EBADENGINE on an adversary-modified root manifest, no node_modules written) tests; deleting the step fails both tests (2 fail); restored, 2/2 pass. (5) missing bootstrapped CLI: the installer matrix gains a bootstrap-succeeds-without-CLI case asserting refusal before ci plus prefix and cache cleanup; reverting the fixture to always write the CLI fails it ('Missing expected exception: private/missing'); restored, 4/4 pass. (6) fallback after successful install: the alert matrix gains NPM_READY=true, npm ci succeeds, npm run fails -> fallback issue; the regression that attempts the script only when installation fails makes that case fail; restored, 1/1 pass. (7) Windows fixture: the Node twin is now a hard link (copy fallback across volumes) on win32 and a symlink elsewhere; the suite asserts the twin is executable. Reverting to an unconditional file symlink only reproduces on Windows (EPERM without Developer Mode), so Windows CI running the release-runtime suite on the pushed head is the witness; Linux cannot deny symlink privilege.

value.text: Round 6 plan (head bb688ba, 6 findings). (3) --location/-L join the scanner's value flags plus corpus cases. (4) npm exec/x with --package/-p are package-acquiring: the install guards and the retry-loop guard (same detector) reject them, while plain 'npm exec <name>' without --package stays allowed per the existing must-allow corpus. (5) the generated bootstrapped CLI records NPM_CONFIG_CACHE per invocation; the matrix asserts the post-bootstrap probe and the ci call both used the private cache. (6) the POSIX PATH fixture npm becomes a quoted sh wrapper (a shebang cannot carry an execPath with spaces) and the matrix bin directory gains a permanent space in its name, so spaces are adversarially exercised on every run. (1)+(2) declined with evidence per the scope control: pinning the caller's Node for the matched CLI and discovering an npm CLI outside the Node directory both need a shim-target discovery mechanism (PATH scan plus cmd parsing or symlink classification) whose success paths cannot be exercised off Windows, conflicting with the 100 percent coverage gate, the no-shell subprocess contract and the ban on trusted sources importing test modules; official Node distributions bundle the npm CLI beside node.exe, which covers every environment the runtime actually executes in. Smallest shipped improvement: a clear refusal naming the requirement when the adjacent CLI is absent on Windows, plus a docs sentence and a follow-up item.

value.text: Round 6 fixes and revert proofs (focused: release-runtime 5/5, daily+release-workflow 48/48, adapter+runtime 67/67, 115/115 combined, typecheck clean): (3) --location and -L joined the value flags; removing --location alone makes the corpus accept 'npm --location global ci' (Missing expected exception, 3 tests fail combined with (4)). (4) package-acquiring npm exec/x (--package, -p, --package=x, -p=x) are rejected by the install guards and the retry-loop guard, which share the detector; the shell scanner consumes the 'npm exec' pair as a wrapper prefix, so the contract also reads the raw words candidates skip; plain 'npm exec <name>' without --package stays allowed per the existing must-allow corpus, and reverting the acquisition rule fails the retry-guard and alias-distinguish tests. (5) the generated bootstrapped CLI records its cache per invocation; the matrix asserts the post-bootstrap version probe and the ci call both ran through the private cache (per-row expected counts) and reverts to an empty record on removal.
